care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to understand a bit about your situation.

**First, let me ask about your child:**

1. **How old is your child?** (or if you're asking about multiple children, please tell me about each one)
2. **What is your child's name?** (This helps me keep track if you have multiple children)

The age of your child is important because:
- Children **under 16** automatically qualify (if other conditions are met)
- Children **aged 16-19** may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Children **20 or over** are not eligible for Child Benefit

Please share these details so we can continue with your assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 15 years old and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about your son **Alex**, who is **15 years old** and lives with you.

Since Alex is under 16, he falls into the automatic qualification age category. Now let me check the next requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to check Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work at all)?**

This is important because children working 24 or more hours per week (and not in approved education or training) are not eligible for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. He's just at school like a normal 15-year-old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's completely normal for a 15-year-old. Since Alex doesn't work at all, he meets this requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now the next question:

**Is Alex NOT receiving any benefits in his own right?**

For example, benefits like:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

Children who receive these types of benefits in their own right are not eligible for Child Benefit. Since Alex is just a regular 15-year-old at school, I'm assuming he's not receiving any of these benefits, but please confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a regular teenager.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what I expected. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex in any type of apprenticeship program?**

The rules vary by region:
- **England**: All types of apprenticeships would disqualify him
- **Scotland**: Modern Apprenticeships would disqualify him  
- **Wales**: Most apprenticeships disqualify, except Foundation Apprenticeships which are approved

Since you mentioned Alex is just at school like a normal 15-year-old, I'm assuming he's not in an apprenticeship program, but please confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship. He's just doing his GCSEs at school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is just doing his GCSEs, which is standard secondary education. Let me move forward.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check about **your residency status** (as the claimant):

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

You can meet the residency requirement through several ways:
- You normally live in the UK (this is the most common situation)
- You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- You have pre-settled status and meet certain conditions (working, studying, sufficient resources, etc.)
- You're a Crown servant living abroad

Since you mentioned Alex lives with you at home, I'm assuming you normally live in the UK together, but please confirm your residency situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - I live in the UK with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since you normally live in the UK, you meet the residency requirement. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now about your responsibility for Alex:

**Are you responsible for Alex?**

You can demonstrate responsibility in several ways:
- **Living with the child** (which you've already mentioned you do)
- Contributing to their upkeep (paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards their care)
- Paying maintenance under a court order or agreement

Since you've already told me that Alex lives with you at home, you clearly meet this requirement through the "living with the child" path. Let me proceed.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another family member
- A former partner

Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at a time. If someone else is claiming and you both agree that you should claim instead, that's fine - they would just need to stop their claim. But if there's a dispute about who should claim, HMRC would need to decide.

What's your situation - is anyone else claiming for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since nobody else is claiming for Alex, that's clear. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check about Alex's living situation:

**Which of these applies to Alex?**

1. **In hospital** - Is Alex currently staying in hospital?
2. **In care** - Is Alex in local authority care?
3. **Fostered** - Is Alex being fostered?
4. **Normal living** - Is Alex living normally at home with you (not in any of the above situations)?

Since you mentioned Alex lives with you at home like a normal 15-year-old, I'm assuming option 4 (normal living), but please confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, I should mention - Alex is fostered. I'm fostering him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Ah, thank you for clarifying that important detail! Since you're fostering Alex, I need to check the specific fostering rules.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. This is an important question for fostered children:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words:
- If the council **is paying** you fostering allowances or payments for Alex's accommodation or maintenance, you would **not** be eligible for Child Benefit
- If the council is **not paying** towards his accommodation or maintenance, you **can** claim Child Benefit

What's your fostering arrangement - is the council paying you for Alex's accommodation or maintenance?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't get anything from the council to foster him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying. So the council is not paying you for Alex's accommodation or maintenance. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You've confirmed that the council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance. Let me now proceed to the final determination.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Based on all the information you've provided, let me record the final eligibility determination:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News - You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit!

Based on the assessment, **you meet all the eligibility requirements** to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

### Why You're Eligible:

✅ **Alex qualifies as a child** - He's 15 years old (under 16)  
✅ **Not working** - He's attending school doing his GCSEs  
✅ **Not receiving benefits** - Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own right  
✅ **Not in an apprenticeship**  
✅ **You meet residency requirements** - You normally live in the UK  
✅ **You're responsible for Alex** - He lives with you  
✅ **No competing claims** - Nobody else is claiming for Alex  
✅ **Council not paying** - Crucially, the local council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance, which means you as a foster carer can claim Child Benefit

### Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate

### Important to Know:

💷 **High Income Child Benefit Charge**: If you or your partner earns over £60,000, you may need to pay a tax charge. You can still claim but may need to repay some or all of it through your tax return.

📅 **Payment frequency**: Payments are made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

### Apply Here:
**https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim**

Do you have any questions about the application process or anything else?
